record.original_question: Does there exist an integer sequence that is good for 2-recurrence of powers of a single transformation but is not good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Is there a sequence that is good for 2-recurrence of powers but is not good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. By a measure-preserving system we mean a quadruple $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ where $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ is a probability space and $T\colon X\to X$ is an invertible measurable transformation that preserves $\mu$. More generally, a system with two commuting transformations is $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T_1,T_2)$ where $T_1,T_2$ are invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ satisfying $T_1T_2=T_2T_1$.

Given a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers $S=(s_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, we say that $S$ is:

(a) good for 2-recurrence of powers (of a single transformation) if for every measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and every set $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T^{-s_n}A\cap T^{-2s_n}A\bigr)>0;$$

(b) good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations if for every system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T_1,T_2)$ with $T_1,T_2$ commuting measure-preserving transformations and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{-s_n}A\cap T_2^{-s_n}A\bigr)>0.$$

Question. Does there exist a strictly increasing sequence $S=(s_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of positive integers that is good for 2-recurrence of powers of a single transformation but is not good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations?
artifact.status_search_result: A direct web search did not turn up a published resolution of this specific question. Related problems on multiple recurrence with commuting transformations and on recurrence along powers of sequences have continued to attract attention (e.g., works by Frantzikinakis–Host, Frantzikinakis–Lesigne–Wierdl, Chu, Assani–Moore, and recent counterexamples of 2025 in the non-commuting setting), but no source consulted reports a sequence good for 2-recurrence of powers yet not for commuting transformations, nor a proof that none exists. Status appears to remain unresolved, but this could not be confirmed with full certainty.

status_evidence.title: Multiple recurrence and convergence without commutativity (Frantzikinakis, 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multiple recurrence for non-commuting transformations and discusses gaps between single-transformation and commuting-transformation cases.
status_evidence.claim: The contrast between recurrence for powers of one transformation and for two commuting transformations is an active area without a definitive separation result.

status_evidence.title: Powers of sequences and recurrence (Frantzikinakis, Lesigne, Wierdl)
status_evidence.snippet: Recurrence properties along k-th powers of integer sequences are studied; behavior across powers can be largely independent.
status_evidence.claim: The literature distinguishes recurrence behavior along sequences and their powers, which is the broader context of the question.

status_evidence.title: Counterexamples to double recurrence for non-commuting deterministic transformations (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides counterexamples for double recurrence in non-commuting cases, but does not address the powers-vs-commuting separation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses related double recurrence questions but not the specific separation asked here.
